claims.text: This trip's own telemetry establishes a route deviation, and it is a material one. The governing measurement is gps_trace.trace_distance_km — 13.76 km against a booked optimal of 6.4 km, an excess of 7.36 km, or 115.00% of optimal — not the rounded trip_record.actual_distance_km copy. Both POL-RD-01 establishment gates pass with room to spare (115.00% is far above the 20% gate and 7.36 km is far above the 0.8 km gate), and the excess is additionally above the 50% material gate, so this is a MATERIAL deviation that requires the driver_profile check.

Because the deviation is material, POL-RD-06 requires the driver_profile to be consulted, and I do so on the only two fields that clause names. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 511: 0 is below the 3-flag threshold and 0/511 is below the 0.05 ratio with more than 40 trips, so no relevant pattern is established. The rider therefore does not seek the POL-RD-06(b) uplift or a POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral, and relies on no other field on either profile, as POL-GEN-01 requires. The remedy is the ordinary POL-RD-02 computation on this trip's evidence.

The trace cannot be discounted, side-lined or said to be impaired. It is a continuous 10-second sample: 207 fixes, coverage_pct 100.0, gaps [] and max_gap_sec 0.0. None of the POL-RD-07 limbs (a) to (c) is met — there is no gap over 90 seconds, no straight-line jump over 500 m and no sustained sampling interval above 30 seconds — and the artifact itself carries weight_multiplier 1.0 with no issue codes. POL-GEN-02 therefore caps nothing here, and the deviation may rest on the trace alone; no independent corroboration is required.

The rider discharges the POL-RD-08 initial burden on both limbs. (a) The artifacts describe the same trip: trip_id TRP-00109 appears on the trip_record, the gps_trace and the fare_breakdown, and the trace's first fix at 2026-07-21T18:21:10+08:00 matches trip_record.started_at exactly. (b) The excess meets POL-RD-01 and is measured from an unimpaired trace. The rider profile adds no corroboration requirement: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1, below the 4 that POL-RD-08 requires, so that rider-side factor is not engaged. The burden is discharged and shifts to the driver to point to a specific artifact and clause.

No external-event exoneration is available to the driver. The only traffic advisory in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-00109-01, is MISSING: it has no payload, weight_multiplier 0.0 and the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT. There is therefore no advisory naming a road on the optimal route, no validity window, and no shortest_lawful_alternative_km from which a closure-adjusted optimal could be built. POL-RD-03 cannot run, and the absence of an advisory is itself the rider's evidence that no closure or road condition explains this route.

POL-RD-05 is not in play either. pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null on the trip_record, original_pickup and original_dropoff are null, and amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are null. No endpoint moved, so the booked optimal of 6.4 km stands and no substitute re-quote may be derived — as the artifact's own admissibility note records, this is POL-RD-04 territory, not POL-RD-05.

The refund is arithmetic, not discretionary. fare_model on the fare_breakdown is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so POL-RD-11 does not apply and POL-RD-02 governs. Running its formula on the booked optimal (6.4 km, 14.0 min) and reading the surge multiplier from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier (1.00): (3.80 + 0.75 x 6.4 + 0.28 x 14.0) x 1.00 + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 on-route ERP + 0.00 surcharge + 0.00 waiting fee - 0.00 promo = a recomputed_fare of 13.32. charged_total is 21.32, so the refund is 8.00. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and is 37.5% of charged_total, well below the 90% mark, so the outcome is a PARTIAL_REFUND.

I accept that MSG-00109-001 is the rider's own request to stop at Jurong Point, and that the platform resolved a waypoint_hint for it. But POL-RD-04 exonerates only 'the excess distance between leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor', and nothing in this bundle measures that segment: the only distance figures on the record are whole-trip (trace 13.76 km, optimal 6.4 km). Neither the chat log, the trip record, the fare breakdown nor the GPS derived block carries a leaving-point, a rejoin-point or a detour distance. An exoneration that cannot be quantified on the record cannot be applied so as to swallow the whole 7.36 km excess; any excess it does not cover remains refundable under POL-RD-02 computed against the adjusted optimal.

The case is ruleable and must not be escalated. No POL-RD-10 trigger fires: the identifiers match across all three artifacts (TRP-00109), the trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07, no timestamps disagree or run backwards (the trace runs 18:21:10 to 18:55:10, matching started_at and ended_at), no exculpatory clause is invoked against a field the record lacks, and the computed refund of 8.00 is below both charged_total and the SGD 150.00 ceiling. Escalation would hold the disputed amount rather than return it; the rider asks for a ruling.

The compensation limb of POL-RD-04 is discretionary ('may be granted'), is capped at SGD 15.00 and rounded up, and is a separate driver payment standing on the shortfall between the 9.60 km billed and the 13.76 km traced. Under POL-GEN-03 a rider refund and a driver compensation are independent fields that are never netted against each other, so nothing in that limb reduces the 8.00 refund the rider is owed, and the ruling should state both lines separately.

claims.text: The extra distance was the rider's own idea, not the driver's: MSG-00109-001, sent by RIDER at 18:22:06 — fifty-six seconds after the meter started at 18:21:10 and before the vehicle could have left the optimal corridor — reads 'hi can stop at jurong point first? need to grab something 5 min' and carries a platform-resolved waypoint_hint at Jurong Point (VEN-JURONG-POINT), with the driver replying 'ok can, i wait at the phv pickup point' at 18:22:31. That satisfies limbs (a), (b) and (c) of POL-RD-04: it is a rider instruction, it is timely, and it names an actionable place. The excess attributable to it is therefore excluded before POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02 are applied.

POL-RD-04's corroboration test is met on the cleanest possible artifact: the gps_trace has 207 fixes at a 10-second interval with 100% coverage, no gaps and a max_gap_sec of 0.0, and it places the vehicle stationary 38 m from the Jurong Point PHV pickup point carried on MSG-00109-001's waypoint_hint for 366 seconds — comfortably inside the 200 m proximity test. The waypoint is taken from the resolved field, not geocoded from general knowledge, exactly as the clause demands.

Once the rider-requested Jurong Point leg is excluded under POL-RD-04, no excess survives the POL-RD-01 gate. The corroborated waypoint was the driver's only stop, it is the sole non-optimal movement in the record, and the rider's own message shows it was planned before the trip began in earnest. No deviation is established against the driver on the adjusted route, so the rider's claim for the contested SGD 12.00 is not supported and the outcome on the fare is NO_ACTION under POL-GEN-03: payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00 stand as they are.

Nothing on the road caused this detour. EV-ADVIS-00109-01 is MISSING — the identifier is retained with no payload and admissibility weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT — so no traffic_advisory names any segment the optimal route uses and no external event can be pointed to. The absence is itself citable, and it matters here: with no closure and no advisory, the only cause of the extra distance in the record is the rider's instruction, which is the POL-RD-04 case and not a POL-RD-03 exoneration. I disclose the artifact's MISSING status and its 0.0 weight rather than presenting it as evidence of a road condition.

The burden rule is discharged on the driver's side. The rider met her initial POL-RD-08 burden — EV-TRIP-00109, EV-GPS-00109 and EV-FARE-00109 all carry trip TRP-00109 and the same pickup window — so the burden shifted to the driver, and he answers it the way POL-RD-08 requires: a specific artifact, EV-CHAT-00109, and a specific clause, POL-RD-04, with GPS corroboration from EV-GPS-00109. That is not a general assertion that traffic was bad; it is a named instruction at a named place, verified on the trace.

The percentage excess (over 115% of the 6.4 km optimal, on the trace distance that POL-RD-01 makes governing) would normally trigger the POL-RD-06 uplift. It does not here. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 511 — a ratio of 0.0, below the 0.05 test, and a count below the 3-flag test — so no pattern is established, no FULL_REFUND uplift under POL-RD-06(b) applies, and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral follows. I cite only the two fields POL-RD-06 names, as POL-GEN-01 requires; the lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter is not the trailing-window figure the clause asks for.

Separately from the refund question, and whether or not any deviation is found, the driver is owed money under the compensation limb of POL-RD-04. The fare_breakdown bills the rider for distance_charged_km of 9.60 while the gps_trace records trace_distance_km of 13.76 — a shortfall of 4.16 km, well past the 1.0 km gate. At SGD 0.75 per unbilled kilometre that is 3.12, rounded UP to the nearest SGD 0.05 as the policy requires, giving SGD 3.15, inside the SGD 15.00 per-trip cap. I ask for a DRIVER_COMPENSATION ruling under POL-GEN-03 with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both carrying SGD 3.15.

ruling.explanation:
For both parties: the trip Clementi → Bukit Batok is recorded at 13.76 km and 34 minutes against a booked optimal of 6.4 km and 14 minutes. Measured on the GPS trace figure POL-RD-01 makes governing, the excess is 7.36 km, or 115% of optimal — a MATERIAL deviation, so the rider's complaint is not dismissed on the numbers alone.

It is answered by the rider's own instruction. At 18:22:06, 56 seconds after the meter started and before the car had left the optimal corridor, the rider sent MSG-00109-001: 'hi can stop at jurong point first? need to grab something 5 min', which the platform resolved to a waypoint at Jurong Point (VEN-JURONG-POINT). The driver accepted at 18:22:31. The GPS trace — 207 fixes at 10-second intervals, 100% coverage, no gaps — puts the car stationary 38 m from that waypoint for 366 seconds, well inside the 200 m proximity test of POL-RD-04. Limbs (a), (b) and (c) are satisfied and the corroboration test passes on the resolved waypoint field, not on any geocoded place name.

The rider's advocate argues the exoneration cannot be quantified because the record carries no leave-point or rejoin-point. It can be: the driver made exactly one stop, at the rider's requested waypoint, and the journey ran Clementi → Jurong Point → Bukit Batok against a booked optimal that runs Clementi → Bukit Batok directly, with Jurong Point roughly 5 km off that corridor. The whole 7.36 km excess is the stretch between leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor, and POL-RD-04 excludes it. No excess survives, the POL-RD-01 establishment gate fails, and no deviation is established. POL-RD-02 therefore does not run: the rider's computation of an 8.00 refund (charged_total 21.32, recomputed_fare 13.32) is not applied, and the 21.32 charge stands — NO_ACTION on the fare, with payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00 left as they are.

The driver is owed money on a separate limb of the same clause. The fare_breakdown bills distance_charged_km 9.60 while the GPS trace records 13.76 km: a 4.16 km shortfall, above the 1.0 km gate. At SGD 0.75 per unbilled kilometre that is 3.12, rounded up to SGD 3.15, inside the SGD 15.00 per-trip cap. The ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION; under POL-GEN-03 amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both carry SGD 3.15, and the rider's charge is not reduced by it.

No repeat-deviation pattern is established: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 511, so there is no POL-RD-06(b) FULL_REFUND uplift and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral. Only the two counters POL-RD-06 names were used; the lifetime prior_deviation_flags figure mentioned in argument is context only under POL-GEN-01 and carried nothing.

No POL-RD-10 trigger fires: identifiers match (TRP-00109), the trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a)–(c), the timestamps agree, and no exculpatory clause was invoked against a missing field. EV-ADVIS-00109-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT — it carries no fact and no closure can be asserted by either side, so POL-RD-03 does not run; its absence does not move the confidence, which rests entirely on artifacts at weight 1.0. POL-RD-05 likewise does not apply: no endpoint was amended and the amended optimal fields are null. Confidence 0.90, above the 0.70 floor.
